unreadable.title: Gears Of War: E-Day–How’s It Selling? Let’s Unpack Things

facts.context: Xbox console exclusive Gears of War: E-Day is reportedly off to a soft start after reaching an estimated 230,000 copies sold in its first week.
Of the nearly 2 million to launch Gears of War: E-Day through Game Pass, 722,000 users are believed to have paid the extra $30 to upgrade to its Premium Edition to unlock early access.
Revenue earned through the Xbox ecosystem reportedly amounted to $27 million, with total earnings reaching about $37 million.
In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70.

The Xbox company told IGN at the time that the model "offers gamers and game creators more choice and opportunity in how they discover, experience, and deliver games."

While Microsoft has yet to confirm official sales data, and it's unclear how Gears of War: E-Day may have driven new Game Pass subscriptions, slow sales could sour an otherwise successful launch.
However, around 950,000 people paid something to get into E-Day, including 722,000 players who dished out an extra $30 to access the game early via its Premium Edition.

This includes a significant number of players who played the game through Game Pass, but it still leaves the title at around $58 million generated since launch, with the numbers rapidly mellowing out and plateauing.

You see, owners of the Premium Edition that costs $99.99 were allowed to fend off the hordes early - from the 1st of October - but Game Pass subscribers could and still can drop a cheaper $30 for the Premium Edition upgrade and all its add-on extras.
